newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - Ahold globalizes with Brazil deal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Ahold globalizes with Brazil deal.

text.p: Dutch food retailer Ahold NV underlined its global ambitions on Monday by announcing plans to take 50 percent of Brazilian supermarket chain Bompreco, its first foray into South America.

Ahold has annual sales of about $24 billion in the U.S., the Netherlands and other European countries. Bompreco is Brazil's fourth largest food retailer and market leader in the country's northeast with annual sales of some $1.4 billion.
Board member Fritz Ahlqvist said the deal reflected Ahold's plans to become one of the world's leading food retailers.
"We already have very strong operations in Europe and the United States and have started in the emerging markets of Asia.
"This opportunity to join forces with a highly respected and successful Brazilian company provides a flying start for Ahold in Latin America," he said.
Analysts said the planned acquisition was a surprising and daring move.
"With this step, Ahold has gained a foothold in Latin America's biggest and most developed market," said ING Barings' Dennis Jullens.
Earlier this year, Ahold roughly doubled its turnover in the U.S. by acquiring the U.S. supermarket chain Stop & Shop.
It has also recently expanded into Asia where it has set up joint ventures in Thailand, Malaysia, Singapore and China.
The Dutch group said it would finance the latest acquisition from its available funds but gave no further financial details.
It said the deal would not dilute earnings in the first year and was expected to enhance earnings per share thereafter.
Though most analysts were upbeat about the Brazil deal, some worried it would expose Ahold to the consumer credit business.
Bompreco runs a customer loyalty programme, offering customers a credit card that can also be used in some 16,000 third-party retail outlets in northeastern Brazil.
"Ahold does not have any experience in financing," John David Roeg from Bank Labouchere said. "It could turn out very profitable, but it's also a bit risky," he said.
Ahold said it and Bompreco planned considerable expansion in the north and northeast of Brazil in the coming years.
The Brazilian company currently operates seven hypermarkets, 29 supermarkets, 11 minimarkets and three department stores that will be remodelled into hypermarkets.
The stock market reacted positively to the news, with Ahold shares rising 1.40 guilder to close at 101.20 on Monday.
